purpose: Bound which landed NIVGEN buffers can consume payload retained from an earlier NIVTEST process when the release-tag Noctis generator follows its published allocation and generation order.

source_boundaries.boundary: All 64,800 s_background bytes are filled with sky_brightness before create_sky and the horizon pass; the scored extent is 46,080 bytes.
build_surface fills txtr[0..65534] with 16 before any planet-type arm; the scored extent is 65,024 bytes.
build_surface fills all 40,000 p_surfacemap bytes with zero before any planet-type arm; the scored extent is all 40,000 bytes.
build_surface clears all 40,000 objectschart bytes and initializes every object's three class fields before the terminal inclination distribution.

known_cross_allocation_read.operation: For ptr 0..39999, object density reads p_surfacemap[ptr+1] and p_surfacemap[ptr+200]. The final 200 ptr+200 reads are beyond the 40,000-byte heightmap.
known_cross_allocation_read.observed_layout_effect: With the retained 16-byte post-heightmap gap, those reads cover the 16 gap bytes followed by the first 184 bytes of the already initialized current object chart.
known_cross_allocation_read.writes: The loop writes only objectschart nr_of_objects fields. It does not write the heightmap, texture, or sky. The source resets both random generators at lines 2641-2642 before historical-ruin placement.

conclusion: Under the published 2.3 generator order, a prior process's payload in the four scored landed buffers is erased before the scored result is produced. The known post-heightmap overread can make the current object chart depend on allocator/header gap bytes, but it cannot alter the already generated sky or texture and does not write the heightmap. Therefore generic same-address payload survival alone cannot explain the residual heightmap, texture, or sky hashes through this source-shaped path. It remains relevant to object-chart discrepancies. The unpublished NIVTEST harness may introduce a different capture, copy, scratch-buffer, or hash boundary, so paired shared-session/clean-session regeneration with raw pre-hash buffers remains decisive; this report does not establish artifact corruption or rule out shifted harness-specific copies. No expected hash, target byte, alternate offset, or parameter value was searched.
